comments.text:
I'm not clear on the distinction between knowledge entries and wiki pages. It seems slightly like wiki pages are more human-facing? However, idk if I think that makes sense. The critical part of a wiki is its graph structure and the connections between pages. Knowledge entries should certainly be interlinked, indexed, well-structured, etc. I think I'd prefer to remove the Knowledge entry entity and move it's role onto wiki pages, which should be mostly for agents not humans. Beliefs which get upgraded into proper knowledge through enough verification should either become a new wiki page fully integrated into the broader wiki or become an update to an existing wiki page. The threshold we'll have to decide but should consider citation type, such that a coworld source code citation is very strong but a single replay is very weak. 

Note that in a later comment I talk about reworking the wiki/memory system, so whatever we decide there, the general idea here is that knowledge should be integrated into the agent's broader knowledge base, not stored separately.

replies.author: Claude
replies.text: Adopted. δ = k × the standard error of the candidate–baseline difference at the planned episode count (k = 0.5 default, capped at 1.0), so noisier metrics and smaller evaluations allow more slippage. The noise comes from a stats/metric-noise.yaml record that maintenance recomputes from league and own-XP data with a deterministic script. See S2 in revision 4.

comments.text: If possible, these shoulde be calculated based on the noise and distributional properties of the game in question from empirical evidence from the league. It should be possible to compute stdev/variance of different metrics from league data, right? Probably that should be part of maintenance and update delta and min-N regularly.
comments.exact: Open What are the slippage tolerance δ and the significance test for the general performance guardrail? What is the minimum N per game?

replies.author: Claude
replies.text: Adopted (same as the δ comment): maintenance computes per-metric variance from league data and our own XP, stores it in stats/metric-noise.yaml, and δ and N derive from it. N comes from a power calculation (80% power, 5% significance by default) for the experiment's minimum effect, with a per-game floor. Significance: a paired bootstrap confidence interval, reported in the Result.
